subject: 1.0.3 broke error message line number reporting

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: 1.0.3 broke error message line number reporting
parts:
Something changed in 1.0.3. that is now preventing
Stan from reporting line numbers and column numbers
of errors:

http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=78

I marked it critical and assigned it to myself. I
suspect the problem arose from the changes Marcus made
to error testing.

I'll also try to figure out how to unit test some
of this behavior. I just hate having unit tests depend
on text messages, since they change, but it's better
than nothing and may prevent this kind of gaff on our
part again.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] 1.0.3 broke error message line number reporting
parts:
Not trying to avoid guilt, but I'm not sure my changes could have done
that. I only touched the code generation bits to spit out try/catch
blocks around the transformed parameter checks, not the actual parser
itself.

If you do construct a unit test for it, git bisect should help you
find the offending change.

Cheers,
Marcus

parts:
Now that I'm looking at the code, I think the
problem is what I did to deal with the R
std::cout and std::cerr access issues. Looks like
things are getting caught too early and rethrown
past where I have access to the right iterator.

Shouldn't be a big deal to fix.

I keep telling myself I'll learn more git, but it always
seems easier to just deal with whatever I've got.

- Bob

Yes, but I don't think that's relevant here. It has
a bunch of non-zero return codes for different kinds
of failures, not that any of them are getting used
anywhere.

The problem is that we're losing the line numbers on
the error reports.

This is all tied up in Boost's crazy iterator scheme.

I've looked further and am now really puzzled as to how
this could've broken at all.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: 1.0.3 broke error message line number reporting
parts:
I was just eyeballing the parser output to judge between good and bad states. But git bisect can be scripted if you have a conclusive way of testing. In this case, my unwritten script would do

make clean-all && make -j8 CC=clang++ /tmp/SU/parser/normal 2>/tmp/parser.log
grep "line=9" /tmp/parser.log

and a successful return code of grep would define the git bisect good state.

Ben
